fills.researcher_notes: SegmentName='Access Northeast Gas Pipeline' (cancelled 2016-17, never got past FERC pre-filing PF16-1-000). The wiki's '36 inches; 42 inches' is a partial summary; FERC's Federal Register Notice of Intent (2016-05-06, reprinting Algonquin's own filed project description for the whole ANE Project) gives the FULL facility-by-facility diameter breakdown: replacement of 45.0 mi of 26-inch pipe with 42-inch (NY/CT); loop extensions of 22.7 mi of 36-inch (Cromwell Loop, Hartford/Middlesex/Tolland Cos CT; Chaplin Loop, Windham Co CT) and 25.9 mi of 30-inch (Q-1 Loop and I-8 Loop, Norfolk Co MA); new 16-inch lateral (26.8 mi, Norfolk/Worcester Cos MA); new 24-inch lateral (2.9 mi, Bristol Co MA). Summed mileage (45.0+22.7+25.9+26.8+2.9=123.3 mi) matches the sheet's LengthKnownKm=197.95 km (=123.0 mi) almost exactly, confirming this ONE row represents the entire multi-state ANE facility set, not just a single loop -- so the full multi-value diameter set (16,24,30,36,42 in) is the correct fill per gem_schema.md's multi-valued-Diameter convention, not just the wiki's two-value summary. offshore-technology.com corroborates the 123.22-mile total length and 'larger diameter pipes' language but gives no inch figures of its own, so it only strengthens the length match, not the diameter tier. Diameter values themselves trace to ONE origin (Algonquin's own FERC filing, reprinted by the Federal Register) -- searched for a second, genuinely independent source with matching inch figures (EIA today-in-energy, Sierra Club/CT Mirror/BEAT fact sheets, Conservation Law Foundation intervenor filings) and found only general project-status mentions (e.g. Enbridge's own FY2017 10-K, itself not independent of Algonquin) with no diameter figures of their own -- so tier stays medium, independent=false, and this note records what was searched. Units already in inches per the row's own DiameterUnits convention (confirmed against P2505 in this same brief, which carries Diameter=24.00 / DiameterUnits='in').
